messages:
Marco: Quick Q — I'll be on unpaid sabbatical for ~6 weeks starting 2026-04-14. How will that affect my HSA contributions/eligibility and the 401(k) employer match? Do I need to enroll now or will payroll deductions just pause? cc @Lina

Lina (People Ops): Short answer: payroll deductions pause when you stop getting paid; employer match only applies to pay periods with employee deferrals. HSA eligibility depends on whether you keep HDHP coverage during the leave (COBRA/paid continuation). If coverage continues, you're still HSA-eligible. If coverage ends, you lose HSA eligibility.

Ajay (Payroll): A few specifics from payroll side: cutoff for changes is the payroll run on 4/1 for mid-April leaves in our cadence (example). If your leave starts 2026-04-14, the last paycheck that will include deductions is the run covering pay date 2026-04-10. If you want a deferral to hit before leave, enroll by 2026-03-31 so it flows on the 4/10 run. We can also try an off-cycle contribution but that's subject to timing and plan rules.

Lina (People Ops): Important on the match: Redwood's match is calculated per pay period. If no employee deferral in a pay period, there is nothing to match for that period. Some plans historically allow catch-up contributions or discretionary adjustments, but Guideline (our plan vendor) typically does not permit retroactive matching for missed pay periods. I'll confirm with rep.

Ajay (Payroll): Payroll codes I'll use: `UNPAID_SABBATICAL` and we tag the employee record with `BEN_PAUSE=Y` so pre-tax deductions stop automatically. If you want to keep making HSA pre-tax contributions while on leave you generally need a vendor-level arrangement (direct debit to HSA or keep payroll deductions via an employer-sponsored continuation). If you go COBRA and elect employer medical continuation, that usually maintains HSA eligibility but does not automatically restart payroll deductions.

Lina (People Ops): Action: I'll open a ticket with Guideline and payroll to check 1) whether a one-time off-cycle contribution can be processed before 4/10 and 2) whether Guideline will allow any retroactive match. Portal link for reference: https://benefits.redwood.ai/ — see Leave & COBRA section. If you want me to request the off-cycle, reply with "please offcycle" and I'll move it.

BenefitsBot: Case #B-2026-874 opened with Guideline. Rep assigned: Nora. Contact: nora@guideline.com.

Marco: Please offcycle — I'd like one last pre-leave HSA deferral and the employee deferral to count for that pay period. Also, if I keep HSA through COBRA, are contributions through COBRA processed pre-tax or would they be after-tax/direct?

Ajay (Payroll): If you enroll in COBRA to continue medical coverage, COBRA itself doesn't change HSA eligibility (still eligible if HDHP). However, payroll pre-tax HSA deductions normally stop when pay stops. If you arrange a direct debit to the HSA provider while on COBRA, those direct contributions are not processed through payroll as pre-tax contributions; you can still make them post-tax and claim the HSA deduction on your tax return (above-the-line). Payroll can do an employer-processed off-cycle pre-tax contribution before your leave starts if we have the enrollment cutoff met.

Lina (People Ops): Confirmed — I'll request the off-cycle now and ask Guideline about retro match. If Guideline denies retro match, we'll document the outcome and discuss options (e.g., one-time voluntary contribution, tax guidance). I'll DM you the ticket link @Marco.

Marco: Awesome, thanks y'all :pray:

Ajay (Payroll): Off-cycle requested. Payroll ref: PR-2219. Scheduled to process by 2026-04-02.

BenefitsBot: Update on B-2026-874: Guideline rep confirmed they can accept the manual contribution for the upcoming run but their match policy is strict — they cannot retroactively apply employer match for missed pay periods. Rep sent confirmation email to Marco.

Marco: Thanks everyone, that helps — appreciate the quick turnaround.
